strategies.text:
Overview

Mega Garchomp is a valuable addition to solo raids. This solo consists of various strategies depending on Mega Garchomp's moveset & the weather. We'll cover this strategy at first with no weather boost and later include special cases involving sunny and windy scenarios.

These routes prioritize absorbing energy on Kyurem Black, the key factor pushing it past Kyurem White, despite it's disadvantage of Dragon tail vs Ice Fang. Mud Shot/Sand Tomb is the exception as it deals too little damage.

Est Time to Win: Varies [150s - 280s]

Main Strategies

1) Hot-Swap Route [Moderate TTW, Casual]

The Hot-Swap route is against:

  1. Fire Blast* [140 | 4.0s AD]
  2. Twister [50 | 3.0s AD]
  3. Breaking Swipe* [45 | 1.0s AD]
  4. Sand Tomb [60 | 4.0s AD]

Simply DPS with Kyurem White or Black. Make sure to fully use every Freeze Shock or Ice Burn without fainting. Breaking swipe is deceptively strong due to its speed & super effective damage, see the note below.

Against Breaking Swipe*

  1. When Kyurem Black/White reaches 30-40% health, it is recommended to swap instead of gambling deeper for more TDO.

Against Fire Blast*

  1. It can be worth dodging if it causes energy to overflow beyond 100. Swapping also works.


2) Catch Tank [Very fast TTW, Some Mechanics]

The Catch Tank route is against:

  1. Earthquake [140 | 3.5s AD]
  2. Outrage [110 | 4.0s AD]

How to Catch tank:

Step 1) A healthy Kyurem Black is swapped in, intercepting these charge moves.

Step 2) It'll cast 1-3 dragon tails, followed by Freeze Shock for enormous damage.

Step 3) The injured Kyurem Black is swapped out; original active attacker (Kyurem white or Kyurem black) comes back in.

Repeat until there are no more catch tanks to continue.


3) Niche Cases

Sunny Earthquake & Dragon Tail: Deals ~(180-185) + ~(24-25) damage to level 45-40 Kyurem Blacks respectively. Most Kyurems under level 44.5 do not survive this combo with level 45+ comfortably surviving past the 1st chained dragon tail.

For battle parties with Level 44 or less, it is recommended to dodge the chained dragon tail or alternatively dodge the earthquake all together.

For battle parties with level 44.5 or over, catch tanking as normal is viable.

Overview

Mega Garchomp is a valuable addition to solo raids. This solo consists of various strategies depending on Mega Garchomp's moveset & the weather. We'll cover this strategy with windy scenarios.

These routes prioritize absorbing energy on Kyurem Black, the key factor pushing it past Kyurem White, despite it's disadvantage of Dragon tail vs Ice Fang. Mud Shot/Sand Tomb is the exception as it deals too little damage.

Windy can make the raid difficult namely due to Mega Garchomp's access to Dragon tail and Breaking Swipe and Outrage. Otherwise this the other strategies remain the same.

Est Time to Win: Varies [150s - 280s]

Main Strategies

1) Hot-Swap Route [Moderate TTW, Casual]

The Hot-Swap route is against:

  1. Fire Blast* [140 | 4.0s AD]
  2. Twister [50 | 3.0s AD]
  3. Breaking Swipe* [45 | 1.0s AD]
  4. Sand Tomb [60 | 4.0s AD]

Simply DPS with Kyurem White or Black. Make sure to fully use every Freeze Shock or Ice Burn without fainting. Breaking swipe is deceptively strong due to its speed & super effective damage, see the note below.

Against Breaking Swipe*

  1. When Kyurem Black/White reaches 30-40% health, it is recommended to swap instead of gambling deeper for more TDO. In fact, with Kyurem Black it is ideal to play 1 Freeze Shock then swap next (especially against dragon tail)

Against Outrage:

  1. It is worth dodging due to the KO potential.

2) Catch Tank [Very fast TTW, Some Mechanics]

The Catch Tank route is against:

  1. Earthquake [140 | 3.5s AD]

How to Catch tank:

Step 1) A healthy Kyurem Black is swapped in, intercepting these charge moves.

Step 2) It'll cast 1-3 dragon tails, followed by Freeze Shock for enormous damage.

Step 3) The injured Kyurem Black is swapped out; original active attacker (Kyurem white or Kyurem black) comes back in.

Repeat until there are no more catch tanks to continue.

strategies.text:
Overview

Without Kyurem Black/White, a diverse pool of counters can be accessed. This now includes some Dragon types where their signature moves are strong enough to compete against typical ice counters. Mega-Garchomp can still be comfortably solo'd but now with a noticeably slower time.

These counters are listed in a separate battle party (named Various Counters).

Est Time to Win: Varies [230.0s-280.0s]


Main Strategies

1) Hot-Swap Route [Moderate DPS, Casual]

The Hot-Swap route is against:

  1. Twister [50 | 3.0s AD]
  2. Breaking Swipe* [45 | 1.0s AD]
  3. Sand Tomb [60 | 4.0s AD]

Simply DPS and swap to the next attacker when the active attacker cannot continue.


2) Dodging [Low DPS, Slightly Mechanical]

The dodge route is typically against:

  1. Outrage [110 | 4.0s AD]
  2. Earthquake [140 | 3.5s AD]
  3. Fire Blast* [140 | 4.0s AD]

Fire Blast is lethal to Shadow Mamoswine/Weavile (Dodge recommended)

Earthquake is lethal to Shadow Mamoswine/Eternatus/Shadow Weavile (Dodge recommended)

Outrage is lethal to Shadow Weavile.

To get a full idea of how much damage these pokemon will take from certain moves visit the catch tank / DPS calculator


3) Catch Tanking [High DPS, Mechanical]

Because of the long animations from each move, Mega Garchomp is great practice to for beginner catch tanking. Garchomps heavy charge move animations last between 3.5-4.0s. Whereas the above counters have charge moves with animations lasting at most 2.5s. Only Mega Mewtwo Y's Ice beam is slower; at 3.5s AD.

The catch tank route is typically against:

  1. Outrage [110 | 4.0s AD]
  2. Earthquake [140 | 3.5s AD]
  3. Fire Blast* [140 | 4.0s AD]


Any/Outrage: Caught comfortably by Eternatus, Mamoswine, Mega Ray

MS/Outrage: Any of the above, Shadow Mamoswine, Palkia Origin

---

Any/Earthquake: Mamoswine

MS/Earthquake: Any of the above, Palkia Origin, Baxcalibur

---

Any/Fire Blast: Baxcalibur
